title: Condition Resistance Decisions
lede: Every ordinary condition should be resistible, each system should resist conditions its own way (your table, docs/SYSTEM_IDENTITIES.md), and dishes are eaten only out of combat. Mark each item. Nothing is built until you do. Notes go to whoever builds it.

meta.label: Prepared by
meta.text: Claude, with 2 brainstormers and 1 design antagonist

groups.title: Build now
groups.note: Matches rules you already stated. No save version change. Yes means it goes to a builder next.

groups.title: Your calls
groups.note: Each item says what Yes and No mean.

groups.title: The seven you are reviewing
groups.note: You said you would look at these again. Yes = make it resistible (say how in the note: through an element, or its own resistance). No = no resistance, like fasting. Later = still deciding.

groups.title: Problems found elsewhere
groups.note: Not cooking. Found while checking. Yes queues a fix.

items.title: Dishes can only be eaten out of combat
items.summary: Your table says cooking is eaten only out of combat. Today the game lets you eat during a fight.

note.label: Plan
note.text: Eating a dish during a fight is refused ("Not during a fight."). The 1.5 s gap between chained hunt fights and the rest break count as out of combat. Pressing Eat during a fight queues one dish: "Eat after this fight". It is eaten on the first out-of-combat moment, and waits out a knockout recovery. A dish already active when a fight starts keeps running. Flasks and the Healing Salve are unchanged.

fields.label: Cost
fields.text: No top-up during a boss fight. Plan the meal before the pull. One extra click if you queue.

fields.label: Offline
fields.text: Nothing is eaten while you are away until consumable automation exists (planned). A dish eaten before you leave keeps running.

fields.label: Queue
fields.text: UI state only, not saved. Checked again when it fires (stock, cooldown).

lines.label: Found
lines.text: A queued dish would have fired during knockout recovery, where statuses run 5x faster and burn the dish. Now it waits.

items.title: Dishes stop clearing bleeding
items.summary: A dish that restores health heals as a 'salve' today, and a salve heal removes bleeding, lacerated, concussed and blaze burn. That is alchemy's job (the Salve), not cooking's.

note.label: Plan
note.text: Health restored by a dish uses a new heal type, 'meal', which clears nothing. Only dishes are affected: the bought Healing Salve keeps clearing wounds. The two dishes affected are Herb-Rubbed Meat and Feast Platter; neither promises wound closing in its text.

items.title: Mark conditions that have no resistance, and check the rest
items.summary: fasting, flat_footed, surprised, toll_steam, toll_ice and toll_overdrive get an explicit "no resistance" mark with a reason. A content check then requires every harmful condition to either have an element (so it is resisted) or carry the mark.

note.label: Plan
note.text: The seven you are reviewing sit on a waiting list the check accepts. The list can only shrink, so a new harmful condition cannot be added without choosing. Immunity cannot be granted to a condition marked as having no resistance (a boss phase cannot be switched off). The forge editor gets the field.

items.title: Monster damage ticks use the same resistance as everything else
items.summary: A condition's damage ticks on a monster still read the monster's declared resistance only. Whether a condition lands already reads the full value (with tag-based resistance). On the player, ticks leave out the elemental resistance stat.

note.label: Plan
note.text: Both read the full value. Checked: no monster that spawns anywhere today changes. Only two unplaced monsters would.

items.title: Condition tooltips say what resists them
items.summary: A condition's tooltip gets one line: "Resisted by: Slashing resistance 10%". It shows your real total, or "Immune" when you are at 100% or more.

note.label: Why the real total
note.text: Your damage resistance is capped at 75% in the stat panel, but immunity reads the full value. Showing 75% while a condition never lands would mislead.

items.title: Should resistance slow down conditions that build by stacks?
items.summary: Bleeding turns into Lacerated after 5 cuts, whatever the target's slashing resistance. Resistance makes each bleed weaker but never delays the laceration. A current test locks this in on purpose: "the number of applications IS the mechanic".

note.label: Yes / No
note.text: Yes: the stack count needed grows with resistance (5 cuts become 10 on a 50% slashing slime, 6 to 7 on floor 2 to 3 automatons, 3 on a slashing-vulnerable target). No: keep today's rule. I recommend No unless you want that change.

items.title: Anupama's two hunger conditions: keep dark resistance working on them?
items.summary: Both belong to Anupama's unique set (like fasting) but carry the dark element, and their data says dark resistance blunting them is deliberate.

note.label: Yes / No
note.text: Yes: mark them as having no resistance, like fasting (dark resistance stops working on them). No: leave them resistible by dark resistance, as now.

items.title: Resistance to one condition, separate from its element
items.summary: Today resisting bleeding means resisting all slashing damage. This adds a second kind: "Bleeding resistance 20%", which adds to Slashing resistance but only for that condition (34 condition families). A dish, flask or charm could then resist one condition without touching damage.

note.label: Yes / No / Later
note.text: Needed if any of the seven becomes resistible without an element (the two psionic ones have no element to use). Yes: build it. Later: decide with the seven. No: element resistance stays the only kind.

items.title: Limit how many dishes are active at once
items.summary: With no limit, several dishes plus a flask, a ward and gear can make you immune to 4 to 6 element families for over 10 minutes.

note.label: Yes / No
note.text: Yes: at most 3 dishes active. Each dish is one slot with everything it gives, its Signature included. A 4th replaces the dish with the least time left. A skill or mutagen can raise the limit later. No: no limit.

items.title: Which sources may make you immune
items.summary: Any status can add resistance today, so a dish, a flask, a divine blessing or a music effect can push you to 100% while it lasts. Gear alone cannot go past the 75% cap; only mutagens raise the cap.

note.label: Yes / No
note.text: Yes: temporary immunity can come from any status while it lasts; permanent immunity only from mutagens (raising the cap, or a gene that grants immunity). No: say in the note which sources should not.

items.title: Monsters get penetration by tier
items.summary: Monsters have no penetration today, so a player at 100% resistance is immune to that monster's conditions forever. With penetration, immunity needs more than 100% as the climb goes on.

note.label: Yes / No
note.text: Yes: 0 on floors 1 to 3, about 0.15 in band 2, set per monster tier. It only affects the 100% line, not how much a partial resistance blocks. No: monsters stay at 0.

items.title: Give the 17 unanswered conditions an answer, per system
items.summary: 17 of the 37 element conditions have no answer in any system a fresh save can use: the whole piercing family, dazed, shard bleed, and the earth, wind, light, arcane and dark conditions.

note.label: Plan
note.text: One answer per system row: slime jellies by element family (cooking round 3), a resistance on a Forges armour recipe (equipment), a divine miracle that turns burning into healing (Flame Vow), and alchemy's cure effects made to work. Yes approves the direction; each piece comes back to you before it is built.

items.title: doused
items.summary: Reached only by another condition turning into it, never applied directly, so a resistance would do nothing unless that changes.

items.title: psionic_compression
items.summary: No psionic element exists. Resistible only through its own resistance (the 'Resistance to one condition' item) or not at all.

items.title: psionic_read
items.summary: Same as psionic_compression: no psionic element exists.

items.title: overgrowth
items.summary: Part of the overgrowth ladder.

items.title: proliferating
items.summary: Reached when an enemy heal escalates. If it becomes resistible, that escalation must stop being charged twice.

items.title: unfolded
items.summary: A divine miracle's mark on enemies. Its effects already touch arcane resistance, so arcane is a possible element.

items.title: queasy
items.summary: From spoiled food (Scorched Mess). If resistible, eating spoiled food must count as something done to you so resistance applies.

items.title: Alchemy hands out divine statuses
items.summary: Frostmoss grants Xima's Rime, Gloomcap grants Veiled and Bloodwort grants Blood Communion. Those are divine statuses. The law says no system uses another's signature conditions.

note.label: Fix
note.text: Give alchemy its own statuses for those three reagents.

items.title: Alchemy's cures do nothing
items.summary: Mendroot promises to cure poison and bleeding, but no condition listens for those cures. Only corrupted listens, for a cleansing that nothing produces.

note.label: Fix
note.text: Make poison and bleeding respond to alchemy's cure tags.

items.title: Every healing flask clears bleeding like the Salve
items.summary: All health-restoring flask forms heal as a 'salve', so a Draught closes bleeding although the alchemy doc says only the Salve cures.

note.label: Choice
note.text: Either the doc changes or the Draught stops clearing wounds. Later: decide with the alchemy item above.

generalNote.label: Anything else
generalNote.hint: Priorities, or anything the items above miss.

blocks.title: Your rules this builds on
items: Alchemy: short consumables, usable any time, in combat.
Cooking: long dishes, eaten only out of combat.
Divine: changes the rules, exclusive, expensive.
Mutagens: change base rules, can exceed limits.
Immune when resistance minus penetration is 100% or more.

blocks.title: No resistance, by your ruling
items: toll_steam, toll_ice, toll_overdrive (the toll collector fight)

footer: Choices save as you click. I read them back before any work starts.
